image_description: A close-up, high-angle shot of a cooked Dungeness crab (Cancer magister) resting on a bed of crushed ice. The crab's carapace is reddish-orange with lighter mottling, typical of cooked crustaceans. Two large, robust chelipeds (claws) dominate the foreground, showing smooth outer shells and dark tips. Several walking legs are visible extending laterally and tucked beneath the body. The background contains blurred elements of other crabs or seafood display cases.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The anterior margin of the carapace is visible between the claws, but the eye stalks are either retracted, obscured by the angle/lighting, or not rendered clearly. No distinct protruding eye structures are visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible portion of the carapace behind the claws shows the correct convex shape and reddish-brown/orange coloration consistent with a cooked Dungeness crab.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image is taken from a dorsal/top-down perspective. The ventral surface (underside/abdomen) is completely occluded by the carapace and legs.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Lighter, creamy-white mottling is clearly visible on the reddish-orange exoskeleton, particularly on the claws and the visible rear carapace edge.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Specular highlights on the claws and carapace indicate a smooth, hard, glossy surface consistent with a calcified exoskeleton.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: While some leg segments are visible on the sides, the full count of five pairs cannot be verified due to occlusion by the large claws and the angle of the shot. Some legs appear fused or indistinct in the lower right.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: First pair modified into robust claws of unequal size with dark tips.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Two large chelipeds are prominent. They appear roughly symmetrical in this view (though natural variation exists), and they feature distinct dark brown/black tips on the dactyls.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Claws have smooth outer surface and serrated inner edges.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The outer surfaces of the claws are smooth. The inner edges (visible where the pincer opens slightly) show textural complexity consistent with serrations/teeth.

artifact_observations.location: Lower right quadrant, junction of legs and ice/background
artifact_observations.reasoning: The distal ends of the walking legs on the right side blend ambiguously into the crushed ice and background elements. There is a lack of clear boundary separation, suggesting slight melting or fusion artifacts common in AI generation of complex overlapping structures.
The crushed ice lacks distinct, sharp crystalline structures. It appears as a soft, cloudy mass with inconsistent refraction, resembling smeared noise rather than realistic ice physics.

The legs on the left side appear to merge into the body wall without clear joint articulation points. The segmentation between individual leg segments is softer and less defined than expected for a hard-shelled crustacean.
